name: p0-ip-only-pulp-i2c-apb3
description: One PULP APB I2C target model, no CPU and no DMA. This target's RTL carries a real, compiled Verilator assertion (i2c_master_byte_ctrl.sv:220, a full_case/parallel_case unique-case check), so the IP-only host drives a legal register sequence and one declared-fault command word with the per-case assertion capture armed. A zero assertion count is then an observation about the declared transaction space, not about a build without assertions.

transactions.note: STATUS after reset: rxack, i2c_busy, arbitration-lost, tip and irq_flag are all clear
CTRL bit 7 enables the core; command writes are ignored while it is clear
STATUS while the start command runs: recorded, not asserted to one value
let the byte controller run with the assertion check active every tick
declared fault transaction: START+STOP+READ+WRITE+ACK+IRQ_ACK in one command word; the RTL command decode keeps priority, so this is an illegal declared command, not an illegal bus beat
declared fault transaction: offset 0x18 is inside the window but outside the six declared registers; the register decode answers with a zero word
